title: Public and private endpoints
learningObjective: Define public and private endpoints and decide when a PaaS service should be reached privately.
foundation: An endpoint is the address a client connects to. A public endpoint is reachable from the internet, for example mystorage.blob.core.windows.net.
A private endpoint puts a network interface with a private IP address from your VNet in front of a service (such as a storage account or SQL database). Traffic stays on the Microsoft network.
With a private endpoint you can turn off public access completely, so the service can't be reached from the internet at all.
engineer: Public endpoints: most PaaS services have one by default. You can restrict them with firewall rules (allowed IP ranges, selected VNets) or disable public network access.

Private endpoints use Azure Private Link: a NIC with a private IP in your subnet maps to a specific resource (for example one storage account), not the whole service. Reachable from the VNet, peered VNets and on-premises over VPN/ExpressRoute.

DNS: clients must resolve the service name to the private IP. Private DNS zones (privatelink.blob.core.windows.net) are created and linked to make this work; otherwise clients still resolve the public address.
Security benefits: no exposure to the internet, protection against data exfiltration (connects to one specific resource), works with NSGs and on-premises connectivity.
Service endpoints (a related AZ-104 topic) keep traffic on the backbone but the service keeps its public IP; private endpoints give it a private IP.

animation.caption: Connect from the internet, the VNet or on-premises with different public-access and private endpoint settings.

example.title: Patient records
body: A hospital stores scans in a storage account. It adds a private endpoint in its app subnet and disables public network access.
The web app in the VNet and clinicians on-premises (over ExpressRoute) reach the account at 10.0.2.5; requests from the internet fail even with a valid key.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription (a free account works)
permissions: Reader to explore; Contributor to create resources
portal: Storage account > Networking > Public network access: Disabled / Enabled from selected networks.
Storage account > Networking > Private endpoint connections > + Private endpoint.
Private DNS zones: privatelink.blob.core.windows.net linked to the VNet.
configuration.cli:
az network private-endpoint create -g <rg> -n pe-st --vnet-name vnet-a --subnet data --private-connection-resource-id <storage-id> --group-id blob --connection-name st-conn
az storage account update -g <rg> -n <account> --public-network-access Disabled

steps: Public vs private endpoint tab: run the default, then each preset.
Public or private endpoint? tab: answer every requirement.
expected: Private endpoint works from the VNet even with public access disabled
The internet can't use a private endpoint
failureScenarios: Disabling public access before the private endpoint and DNS are ready
lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.symptom: VMs still go to the public IP after adding a private endpoint.
troubleshooting.fix: Link the privatelink private DNS zone to the VNet.

troubleshooting.symptom: Internet clients can't reach the account any more.
troubleshooting.fix: Enable selected networks, or use the private path.

comparisons.difference: Private endpoint: private IP for one resource. Service endpoint: optimised route to the public endpoint from a subnet.
VPN connects networks; a private endpoint gives a service an address inside the network.

misconceptions.myth: A private endpoint makes the service private automatically.
misconceptions.reality: Public access stays on until you disable it.

misconceptions.myth: Private endpoints connect to the whole service (all storage accounts).

architectureDecisions: Use private endpoints for data services holding sensitive data.
Disable public network access when all clients are private.
Plan private DNS with the endpoint.
